source.title: How the Incas Built Their Heartland

interpretation: Early Cusco agriculture included maintained canals and terraces before imperial expansion. Northern basin terraces covered hundreds of hectares. Sacred Valley communities also used higher-elevation dry farming and herding; later valley-bottom maize development cannot all be backdated to 1337.

quantitative_evidence.role: order-of-magnitude check, not a complete game-location cultivated-area total
progression/attained-yield context, excluded from automatic starting assignment

next_model_action: Audit zero-crop Pisaq against terrace/crop physics and dated cultivated extent. Do not substitute later imperial hectares or populations for current support.
exclusions: No whole-province irrigation fraction inferred from one site.
No automatic modern or imperial maize yield at game start.
